uncertaintyKind: Formal catalog uncertainty; excludes extra shape, spin and thermal-model systematics. It is not the total uncertainty of the displayed physical scale.
additionalSystematics: Usui2011§2.3 explicitly omits unquantified shape/spin/thermal-model effects; rotation can add a few to about10%in size, especially for fewdetections. No invented numerical confidence interval is assigned to these unquantified effects.
diameterSemantics: Mean fitted diameter of a nonrotating sphere in the modified Standard Thermal Model. Its use as the volume-equivalent diameter of the separate convex DAMIT mesh is an explicit display-scale approximation, not a published physical-volume calibration.
limitations: The physical size is approximately calibrated by assigning the AKARI thermal effective diameter to the mesh volume-equivalent diameter. Neither source mesh nor spin is modified. Convex inversion supplies only broad outline; no resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture can be inferred. Published convex inversion from Hanuš et al. (2016). The selected archive solution is retained as a reproducible coarse model. An alternative pole remains possible; no unique orientation is claimed. The release supplies no registered global surface imagery or measured local terrain. AKARI thermal effective diameter provides only an explicit volume-scale approximation.
visibleDescription: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 37.03 km effective diameter (catalog ±0.61 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size is used as a volume-scale approximation. Both pole solutions remain possible. The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotational phase is illustrative.
